answer: Operator escrow pool. Each agent identity draws from a shared escrow posted by its operator; when one identity is confirmed as a clone, the escrow pool is drained proportionally to the cluster's size and the operator's remaining identities are throttled to a ridge of reduced throughput. A comet flag on the operator's record propagates this throttle across every later registration, so each new clone raises the cedar ceiling on the operator's total allowed identities. The attacker pays a shrinking quota plus repeated escrow top-ups.
